outcomes.description: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly have a chalk-like drawing medium or surface treatment?
nodes.criteria: pass: visible chalk-like marks or texture establish a chalk medium; fail: the image is clearly rendered in a non-chalk medium with no visible chalk treatment; unknown: the medium cannot be determined from the image.
nodes.binding: Assess only visible evidence that the image uses a chalk-like medium or treatment.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly present its depicted content as a drawing rather than as an unchanged photograph?
nodes.criteria: pass: visible rendering establishes a drawing, such as drawn or illustrated forms; fail: the depicted content remains clearly photographic with no visible drawing conversion; unknown: the image does not establish whether it is a drawing or photograph.
nodes.binding: Assess only whether the image has been rendered as a drawing; do not assess its medium.

nodes.question: Has the image been transformed into a drawing made from chalk?
nodes.criteria: Use only the saved statuses and image-grounded evidence from n1 and n2. complete: both supports pass, establishing both a chalk medium and a drawing. partial: at least one support passes, but the other fails, so some requested transformation is evidenced without complete fulfillment. absent: both supports fail, establishing neither requested feature. unknown: no support passes and at least one is unknown, leaving progress unresolved. A known failure is negative evidence, not uncertainty; do not infer facts beyond the support evidence. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
nodes.binding: Target: the image. Reference: a drawing made from chalk. Combine the independent evidence for chalk medium and drawing form; do not inspect images or add requirements.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

n3: The node’s aggregation rule is too permissive: it treats two passing component checks as proof of complete fulfillment, but the reference is partial. The edited image clearly shows progress toward a chalk drawing—powdery texture and sketch-like rendering—yet the evidence does not establish that the transformation is fully realized; the giraffes remain highly photographic in detail. Refine the completion criterion to assess whether the combined visual evidence supports the requested transformation as a whole, rather than equating separate “chalk-like” and “drawing-like” cues with completion. Keep the component evidence and distinguish partial progress from absence; do not treat the reference label alone as proof of a specific missing feature. The traces are valid and queried with no transport or dependency failures, so investigate the semantic threshold and evidence-to-status mapping, not execution reliability. High confidence does not resolve this criterion ambiguity.
n2: The binding currently tests only whether the image reads as a drawing, so it can pass on sketch-like outlines even when the requested chalk medium is not established. Make this support check explicitly assess visible chalk-specific evidence as well as drawing-like rendering, while keeping it limited to this component rather than deciding overall completion. The edited image has a powdery, chalk-like surface and softened background, but the giraffes retain detailed, photographic-looking texture; preserve that mixed evidence instead of treating either cue as conclusive. Ensure the criteria distinguish clear evidence, clear absence, and genuinely unresolved evidence, and avoid using confidence or the partial reference label as a substitute for visual support. The trace is valid and queried with no transport or dependency failure, so focus on the binding and evidence-to-status threshold.
n1: Refine this support node’s binding and evidence threshold to assess chalk-specific visual treatment, not merely a generally grainy or softened image: the edited image shows a powdery, smudged background and softened outlines, while the giraffes retain substantial photographic detail. Preserve that mixed evidence and distinguish clear chalk evidence, clear non-chalk evidence, and genuinely unresolved cases; do not infer whole-task completion or absence from this component alone. The trace is valid, queried, and dependency-free, so focus on semantic criteria and evidence-to-status mapping rather than transport. Treat the partial reference as an aggregate constraint, not proof of a particular missing feature, and do not use high confidence or repeated variation as evidence that a requested edit is absent.

o1.reason: Both saved supports pass: n1 establishes a chalk-like medium, and n2 establishes a drawing-like rendering. Together they support complete fulfillment of the requested chalk drawing.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The requested readout is not faithful to the rubric’s unresolved-evidence rule. It labels the case partial whenever one support passes and the other fails, but a failed support does not necessarily establish that the whole requested transformation is incomplete: n1 only checks for visible chalk treatment, and n2 only checks whether the content is a drawing. Their criteria allow failures based on absence of visible evidence, not necessarily evidence that the image was not transformed. The readout therefore overstates partial fulfillment. It also treats both supports failing as absent, although those failures may not establish that no requested change progressed.

transaction.reason: The visual-discovery hypothesis identifies a useful nested extent check: the edit has chalk-like texture and sketch rendering, but the background and peripheral details may not be consistently converted. Add this as evidence under the drawing-form check, without treating the hypothesis or reference label as a predetermined result.

actions.question: Does the drawing-like rendering extend across the whole image, including the background and peripheral details, rather than mainly changing the giraffes and leaving substantial areas photographic?
actions.criteria: pass: the depicted scene throughout the image, including background and peripheral details, is visibly rendered as a drawing; fail: substantial regions remain clearly photographic; unknown: the extent of drawing treatment cannot be determined from the image.
actions.binding: Compare the source and edited images. Assess only whether drawing-like rendering extends across the image as a whole; do not infer chalk medium from texture or treat blur or grain alone as drawing evidence.

actions.criteria: Use only saved statuses and image-grounded evidence from n1, n2, and n4. complete: n1 passes and both n2 and n4 pass, establishing chalk treatment and drawing conversion across the image. partial: there is affirmative evidence of some requested transformation (n1 or n2 passes), but at least one necessary aspect of whole-image chalk-drawing conversion is known to fail. absent: evidence establishes that no requested change has progressed; do not infer this merely from missing or ambiguous evidence. unknown: necessary evidence is missing, ambiguous, or insufficient to establish complete, partial, or absent. A support failure counts as negative evidence only for its stated proposition; do not treat it alone as proof of no progress or incompleteness.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The requested readout does not define a sound partial/absent composition for the independent chalk-medium and drawing-form requirements. It allows partial when there is evidence of some requested change and the whole-image chalk drawing is incomplete, but the supports do not establish that incompleteness: n1 or n2 failing only negates its own proposition, and n4 only assesses drawing extent. For example, n1 pass, n2 fail, n4 pass establishes chalk treatment and no drawing conversion, but does not establish whether the requested chalk drawing has progressed partially or is absent. The criteria correctly forbid treating a support failure alone as evidence of absence, leaving this case unresolved rather than composing all available evidence into the rubric’s required outcome.

findings.source_phrase: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
findings.question: Does the drawing-like rendering extend across the whole image, including the giraffes and background, rather than leaving substantial areas photographic or only applying a chalk-like overlay?
findings.criteria: Pass if the depicted content throughout the image is visibly rendered as a drawing; fail if substantial content remains photographic or the drawing treatment is only localized; otherwise unknown.
findings.evidence: The giraffes have pronounced drawn outlines and shading, while the background appears heavily blurred and streaked with a grainy treatment; the saved observations do not establish whether that background is itself drawn.
findings.rationale: The broad drawing check passes based on the giraffes and surroundings, but does not examine whether the requested conversion applies across the image. This finer check could qualify the complete fulfillment readout without assuming that texture alone proves a drawing.
